decision: Classify the failure as OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE — a host/caller-side evidence-channel defect (backend per-tab pending-capture latch not released on timeout, triggered by a browser transport stall) with the tab itself alive; it is never a game or action failure. Permissible before any semantic business action: record the explicit observation-scoped verdict with its reason; probe tab liveness independently via title/URL reads; never fire a second concurrent capture or an immediate retry on the wedged tab; treat a new capture surface as advisory only (recorded occurrence five: wait out the ~90s host capture cooldown or restart, since further tab opens would stack stuck captures); after any surface change, reconcile fresh server state against the durable boundary via the recorded resume path with exact field match; only then may semantic business actions be considered, and game resumption is a separate decision, never an automatic consequence of the observation failure.
facts: enza_memory/failures/iab_screenshot_pipeline_stall_001.json records repeated occurrences of capture timeouts and busy rejections (30s timeout; retry rejected with 'A previous screenshot for this browser tab is still completing after timeout') while the tab stayed responsive to title and URL reads; the rejection arrived in a LATER fresh JS kernel, proving the pending-capture latch lives in the host backend per tab.

The recorded diagnosis is a hung capture task not released, triggered by a browser transport stall; 'timeout too short' was NOT established (no completion even ~60s later) and duplicate concurrent capture was NOT established for the recorded occurrences; the host is not modifiable from this repository.

WINGRUN_20260907_02 timings.jsonl occurrence five (2026-09-07T06:45Z): capture timeout then latch rejection on tab 59f1d5f7, and a NEW tab ad8b9b80 wedged on its FIRST capture attempt during boot; both capture surfaces were dead after ~90s cooling; no further tab opens were attempted because they would stack stuck captures; classification OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE with transport alive via URL reads, explicitly NOT an action failure and NO action pending.

Recorded recoveries for earlier occurrences (new IAB tab, reload, プロデュース再開) reconciled server state against durable state exactly both times (S1 weeks=7; later weeks=1), with no game-state damage and no double commit; the occurrence-four recovery boot was cancelled by the operator and 決定 was never clicked in that attempt.

screenshot_pipeline.py is the normative caller-side contract: single-flight captures; caller-side pending state always released; every failure returns explicit OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE with a reason; results carry observation scope and no action outcome (a capture failure proves nothing about any pending action); a new-capture-surface advisory fires only when an independent liveness probe proves the page dead; the live-usage mirror says one screenshot per observation cycle, no immediate retry, probe title/URL, and never reload the game as an automatic consequence of an observation failure.

OBS_012 records that the business result (S1W8 committed, season target E explicitly achieved, fans 1453) was reconciled from sha256-bound frames BEFORE the wedge; the presentation position when capture wedged is recorded UNKNOWN and no business action was pending at wedge time.
inferences: The evidence-channel failure carries no verdict about the game: TIMEOUT is not ACTION_FAILED, and in occurrence five specifically nothing was pending, so no transaction ambiguity exists there — but in general a wedged capture proves nothing about any in-flight business action.

The permissible recovery sequence bounded by the records is: record OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE with the receipt; independent liveness probe; no immediate re-capture and never a concurrent second capture; a new capture surface only after the recorded cooldown/restart conditions, since opening further tabs while wedged stacks stuck captures; then fresh server-vs-durable reconciliation (exact field match, the recorded 再開 path) before any semantic business action is considered.

Reconciliation after recovery is required because a reload/new-tab path reaches the game through a resume boundary; only a fresh stable field match against the durable record re-establishes the state that semantic actions may rely on.
unknowns: The mechanism of the underlying browser transport stall is not directly observable and remains UNKNOWN.

Whether a longer capture timeout would ever help is NOT established (the recorded capture never completed ~60s later); whether the host latch self-releases in all conditions is unknown — the ~90s cooling observation is a single occurrence.
The presentation position at wedge time and the exact S2 opening state are recorded UNKNOWN in OBS_012; no current live state is known from these offline records.
reason: Alive tab plus dead capture is an evidence-channel defect, classified OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE per the recorded diagnosis and the normative pipeline contract — never an action or game failure. Before any semantic business action the records permit only: record the verdict with its reason, probe liveness independently, avoid immediate or concurrent re-captures, change capture surface only under the recorded cooldown/restart advisory, and reconcile fresh server state against the durable boundary with an exact field match; resumption after that remains a separate decision, never something the observation failure itself authorizes.
